questions.question: What motivated you to go on exchange? (pick the most important one) *
questions.answer: Career opportunities

questions.question: Which aspects were crucial to choosing your study destination? *
questions.answer: I wanted to experience the Australian culture as well as speak the English language more fluently.

questions.question: How would you rate your overall study abroad experience? *
Additional comments:
How easy was it to find the information you needed to know upon arrival? *
questions.answer: It was quite easy. UTS provided help to understand what action steps were important to get started. They send all information via email and offer physical help if needed.

questions.question: What assistance, if any, did you receive when you arrived at your study destination? *
questions.answer: As mentioned before, UTS were very helpful regarding getting international students enrolled and ready for the semester.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the orientation and assistance available to students at your host institution upon arrival? *
Additional comments
How did you find housing? *
questions.answer: I found housing on my own

questions.question: Did you live on campus or off campus? *
questions.answer: Off campus

questions.question: How easy was it to find off campus housing? Any recommendations? *
questions.answer:
It can be tricky since Sydney's housing market is competitive. I recommend using
flatmates.com.au
or Facebook groups to find accommodation, I found my place after 7 days in Sydney.

questions.question: What should future exchange students know about living off campus? *
questions.answer: It is fun to get to know aussies, and not only stay among international students.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the housing available to students? *
Additional comments:
How easy did you find the registration process at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
Please describe the registration process at your host institution *
questions.answer: The choosing of subjects was done before coming to Sydney, but final changes and enrollment were done at UTS. They are helpful if this needs assistance,

questions.question: What kind of help was available? *
questions.answer: They offer help via email or physically through UTS HELPS.

questions.question: How successful were you in registering for the classes you wanted? *
questions.answer: I had to do a few changes, but I was very happy with my subjects. They have many to choose from.

questions.question: What advice would you offer to future exchange students about registration at your host institution? *
questions.answer: Stay on top of your UTS inbox, you will have loads of information coming in. Else, don't feel hesitant to reach out for help if needed.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the academic programme at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
Were you a BA or MA student at UCPH when you were on exchange? *
questions.answer: BA

questions.question: Please elaborate on the level of courses *
questions.answer: I found the content of the subjects to be more industry-focused and easy to understand. I really liked this part. Though, I found the lecturers and tutors to be harder when marking assignments.

questions.question: How did the style of teaching at your host institution compare with that of UCPH? *
questions.answer: It is more focused on how things are done out in the "real world". Less academic.

questions.question: How long were you on exchange? *
questions.answer: 1 semester

questions.question: Please list the courses you were enrolled in during your first semester. *
questions.answer:
Management Skills
Innovation Lab
Introduction to Strategy
Business and Social Impact

questions.question: What specific courses would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: I recommend what I just mentioned. The lectures and tutors did a good job to make us students understand the content.

What unexpected costs did you encounter? *
questions.answer: The city is expensive to live in, but the pay is also high. I recommend finding a pt time/casual job to balance out your costs.

questions.question: What items were more or less expensive than you expected? *
questions.answer: Groceries are a bit more expensive.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the non-academic opportunities (clubs, sports, etc.) at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
What kinds of cultural, athletic and social activities were available for students at your host institution? *
questions.answer: UTS offers a wide array of clubs from sports, to chess, to performance, and so on. Cheap and easy to get started.

questions.question: Which non -academic activities would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: I was in the Dance community, they offer nice classes of different genres.

questions.question: What do you recommend other visiting students see or do on their weekends or holidays? *
questions.answer: There are plenty of day tours to do around Sydney. I liked Karloo Pools, Manly Beach, and the Bondi to Coogee walk. Apart from this, make sure to travel around Australia once you're here.

questions.question: How easy was it to adjust to the local culture of your exchange site? *
questions.answer: Australians are generally very outgoing and happy to engage with "strangers". Be open and join when it is possible. They are easy to be around and I felt good being here culturally right away.

questions.question: Do you have any tips for socializing with local students?
questions.answer: Join UTS clubs, go to the parties, chat with your study group members outside uni.

questions.question: What, if any, cultural differences did you find particularly challenging? *
questions.answer: Australian accents can be challenging to understand, but it's generally not a problem.

questions.question: What parts of the culture did you most appreciate? *
questions.answer: People in Sydney are very outdoorsy and active which I really liked. Also, their coffee culture is next level (and half the price of coffee in CPH). The weather is generally very sunny as well.

questions.question: What are the three most important things you would tell a UCPH student who is going to your host institution on exchange? *
questions.answer:
Be open to new experiences and people
It can be difficult and stressful to get everything organised in the beginning, but it will be all worth it!
Explore everything Sydney (and Australia) has to offer when you can

questions.question: Is there any other information that you think might prove useful to future exchange students attending your host institution? *
questions.answer: UTS is in the center of Sydney and easy to get to no matter which suburb you stay in.

questions.question: What was the most rewarding part of your exchange experience? *
questions.answer: To experience living in another city far away from home, and learn the language even more fluently. Also, all the people that I have met and the opportunities I have gotten.

questions.question: What was the greatest challenge during the exchange? *
questions.answer: The first four weeks were quite challenging. Finding a place to live, setting up phone, getting an Australian bank, etc. can be stressful. But it all works out!

questions.question: Any other comments?
Do you agree to share your travel report with other fellow students? *
questions.answer: Yes
